mem.t: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

lessons.title: The Prodigal Comes Home
lessons.theme: The spiritual life begins not with effort, but with coming home

v: “He arose and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.
The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
“But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let’s eat and celebrate;
for this, my son, was dead and is alive again. He was lost and is found.’ Then they began to celebrate.

lessons.still: Take a deep breath and let it out slowly. Tell the Lord, “Lord, I’m home.” Take the busyness, the guilt and the burdens in your heart and lay them at the Father’s feet, the way a traveller sets down a heavy pack.
teach: Many people think of the spiritual life as a performance review: how many chapters I read, how long I prayed, how many times I slipped up. But the story of the prodigal son tells us that the first step of the spiritual life is not “doing better.” It is “turning around and coming home.”

Notice what the father does: he “saw,” he “was moved with compassion,” he “ran,” he “fell on his neck,” he “kissed him.” All five verbs belong to the father; every move is his. The son has not even finished his rehearsed confession before the father interrupts him and gives him a robe (honour), a ring (authority) and sandals (sonship, for slaves went barefoot).

This is the gospel: God does not wait for us to become good before he accepts us; he accepts us in order to make us good. Change your mindset and your life will change—from “I must work hard to make God love me” to “God already loves me, and I respond to his love.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: The prodigal leaving home is the self-ruled life at its extreme—“Give me my share of the property”—wanting to be his own master. Coming home means stepping down from the throne of self and returning to his place as a son. Humility is the key to revival, and coming home is the first step of humility.
q: Who is God? — From the father’s five actions, what kind of God do you see?
Who am I? — Are you more like the prodigal leaving home, the prodigal on the road back, or the older brother who stayed home while his heart wandered far away?
How shall I respond? — In what one area today do you need to “turn around and come home”?
lessons.jesus: The Jesus who told this parable is himself the embodiment of the father’s heart that “ran.” He left his heavenly home and travelled into the far country to find us; on the cross he was stripped of his clothes so that we could be clothed in the best robe.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, thank you that while I was still far off, you saw me and ran to me. I will no longer try to earn your love with my performance; I confess that I need you. Today I have come home. Please be the Lord of my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write one sentence: “I have come home, because…”
Say something accepting and unconditional to a family member or friend
Before each task today, pray silently: “Father, I’m home.”
lessons.noon: “But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran” — Lord, right now I come back into your arms too.

lessons.title: Seeing Our Problem: Self-Rule
lessons.theme: The root of humanity’s fall is wanting to take God’s place

v: for God knows that in the day you eat it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”

When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took some of its fruit, and ate. Then she gave some to her husband with her, and he ate it, too.
All we like sheep have gone astray. Everyone has turned to his own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.

lessons.still: Be still for a moment and ask the Holy Spirit to shine like a flashlight into your heart: “Lord, search me, and show me the places in me that are centred on myself.” Don’t rush, don’t defend yourself—just let him shine his light.
teach: The heart of the serpent’s temptation is one sentence: “You will be like God.” The problem was not simply eating a piece of fruit. It was that humanity wanted to leave its place as human, grasp God’s power, and decide for itself what is good and what is evil.

This is the self-ruled life: centred on myself, wanting to be my own master and king. Its outward expression is pride. Isaiah puts it even more plainly: “Everyone has turned to his own way.” The essence of sin is that “my way” replaces “God’s way.”

We see our problem not to condemn ourselves but to be healed. It is like going to the doctor: the right diagnosis comes first, then the right prescription. Today’s diagnosis reads: my root problem is not my circumstances, and not other people—it is the “self” inside me that wants to be king.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Pride is leaving our place and grasping power; humility is laying down power and returning to our place—let people be people and let God be God. The focus is not on other people’s faults, but on my own need for the Lord’s light.
q: Who is God? — When God sets boundaries for us, do they come from restriction or from love?
Who am I? — Where recently have you wanted to “decide good and evil” for yourself and be your own master?
How shall I respond? — Which piece of “my way” are you willing to hand back to God?
lessons.jesus: The first Adam said in the garden, “I will be like God.” Jesus, the last Adam, said in the garden of Gethsemane, “Not my will, but yours, be done.” Jesus is the perfect example of the self-emptied life.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that I often turn to my own way, wanting to be my own master and king. Thank you for laying my iniquity on yourself. Please tear down the pride in me, so that I can return to my place as a human being and let you be God. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down one thing where you recently “took charge” yourself, and entrust it to the Lord
When things don’t go your way today, first ask: “Who is on the throne right now?”
Say a humble word to someone you have treated with pride
lessons.noon: “All we like sheep have gone astray. Everyone has turned to his own way.” — Lord, right now I lay down my way and follow yours.

lessons.title: Seeing God’s Grace: The Cross
lessons.theme: God has prepared a complete solution for us

v: For while we were yet weak, at the right time Christ died for the ungodly.
For one will hardly die for a righteous man. Yet perhaps for a good person someone would even dare to die.
But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
for by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God,
not of works, that no one would boast.

lessons.still: Picture yourself standing at the foot of the cross. You don’t need to say anything—just look up. Let that love, given “while we were yet sinners,” slowly fill your heart.
teach: Yesterday we saw the problem; today we see the answer. Paul uses three words to describe our condition: “weak,” “sinners,” and elsewhere, “enemies.” God’s love was not shown when we were most lovable, but when we were least lovable.

The cross dealt with two things: Jesus’ death dealt with both our sins and our sinful nature; Jesus’ resurrection gives us new life. We are not saved by patching up the old life, but by receiving a completely new one.

“By grace… through faith”—grace is the gift on God’s side; faith is the empty hand we hold out on ours. If a gift had to be earned by works, it would no longer be a gift, and people would boast. The gospel takes away every reason to boast and leaves only thanksgiving.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Everything is what God has done and accomplished in Jesus; all of it is God’s grace. So the glory does not go to me but to Jesus. Only through the truth of the gospel can we live the self-emptied life.
q: Who is God? — How does the phrase “while we were yet sinners” help you know God’s love?
Who am I? — Are you still quietly trying to “earn” God’s acceptance with good works?
How shall I respond? — How will you express your thanks today?
lessons.jesus: On the cross Jesus said, “It is finished!” He left no work for us to complete. Our spiritual practice is not finishing our salvation, but resting and responding within a salvation that is already complete.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for dying for me while I was still a sinner. I lay down my own merits and hold out empty hands to receive your grace. From today on, my whole life will be a response of thanksgiving. All glory to you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down three things about the cross that you will thank God for today
Memorise Ephesians 2:8 and repeat it silently three times
Make “Glory to the Lord” your silent prayer as you finish each small task today
lessons.noon: “In that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.” — Lord, right now I look to your grace alone.

lessons.title: A New Creation
lessons.theme: It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me

v: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. That life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me.

lessons.still: Place your hand on your chest and say quietly, “Lord Jesus, you live in me.” Sense his presence—not far away in heaven, but near, in your heart. The Holy Spirit dwells in the heart, not in the head.
teach: A caterpillar does not become a butterfly by working hard at “learning to fly.” It goes through death and new birth inside the chrysalis; its very nature changes, and then it flies naturally. It is the same for Christians: we are not “old selves trying hard to be good,” but “new creations.”

Galatians 2:20 is the manifesto of the self-emptied life: the self-ruled life of the old self has been “crucified with Christ”; the self-emptied life of the new self is “Christ lives in me.” Self-emptying does not mean becoming nothing; it means letting the infinite Christ live out his infinite life in me.

Then why do we still fail? Because we often forget who we are and slip back into the habits of the old self. So our daily practice is to change our mindset again and again: I am already a new creation; today I choose to let Christ live in me.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-emptied life lets Jesus live within; only the self-emptied life lets Jesus reign; only the self-emptied life can be led by the Holy Spirit. The self-ruled life of the old self becoming the self-emptied life of the new self—this is how a defeated life becomes an overcoming life.
q: Who is God? — “Who loved me, and gave himself up for me”: how have you experienced this personal love?
Who am I? — In what area are you still living like the “old self”?
How shall I respond? — In what situation today will you let Christ live in you?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “I always do the things that are pleasing to him.” He lived in complete dependence on the Father. Today this same Jesus lives in me, and his life is my overcoming life.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for making me a new creation. The old has passed away; I am no longer defined by my past. Today it is not I who live, but you who live in me. Please reign in my words, my thoughts and my reactions. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: When you face a challenge today, say silently: “No longer I, but Christ.”
Write down one habit of the old self and how the new self would respond instead
lessons.noon: “And it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me.” — Lord, right now please live in me.

lessons.title: Let Jesus Reign
lessons.theme: Denying ourselves to follow the Lord is the freest road of all

v: He said to all, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, but whoever will lose his life for my sake will save it.
Have this in your mind, which was also in Christ Jesus,
who, existing in the form of God, didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped,
but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men.
And being found in human form, he humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, yes, the death of the cross.

lessons.still: Quietly spread out today’s plans before the Lord one by one, like handing over keys to their owner one at a time. Say, “Lord, these are all yours.”
teach: This week we have walked a road: coming home (Day 1) → seeing our self-rule (Day 2) → seeing grace (Day 3) → becoming a new self (Day 4) → and today, letting Jesus reign.

When Jesus speaks of denying ourselves, there are three actions: deny yourself, take up your cross daily, and follow. Notice the word “daily.” Letting Jesus reign is not a one-time decision but a choice we make every morning. A ship can only have one captain; if I don’t step down, the Lord cannot take the helm.

Philippians shows us the heart of Jesus: he existed in the form of God, yet “didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped.” Instead he emptied himself, humbled himself and obeyed. The first Adam grasped at power, wanting to become God; Jesus laid down power and became human. This is humility: laying down power and returning to our place.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The two core values—let Jesus reign; let Jesus receive all the glory. Denying ourselves means living for Jesus and for others, not for ourselves. Humility inspires humility and brings a win for everyone; this is where building what belongs to God begins.
q: Who is God? — What kind of God do you see in the way Jesus “emptied himself”?
Who am I? — Which room of your life does the Lord not yet rule (time, money, relationships, dreams)?
How shall I respond? — Which “key” will you hand to the Lord today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus is the living model of self-denial: he gave up the glory of heaven, gave up his own will, and gave up his own life. He does not merely tell us to walk this road; he walked it ahead of us, and now he lives in us and walks it with us.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, I am willing to deny myself, take up my cross daily and follow you. I give up the throne of my life to you. Please reign over my time, my money, my relationships and my dreams. May you receive all the glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Make a list of “the rooms of my life” and hand each one over to the Lord
Do something small for someone else, not for yourself, and don’t let anyone know
Tomorrow (Saturday), share the grace of this week with a spiritual companion
lessons.noon: “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself.” — Lord, right now I let you reign.
